name: Ron Shaich
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2023)
forbes_bio: Ron Shaich is the chairman of Mediterranean fast casual chain Cava and an investor in multiple fast-casual food brands.
Shaich cofounded the bakery-cafe Au Bon Pain in 1981. With Shaich as its CEO, Au Bon Pain bought the predecessor to Panera Bread in 1993.
In 2017, Shaich sold Panera to JAB Holdings for $7.5 billion; he pocketed nearly $400 million (pre-tax) from the sale.
The next year, Shaich reinvested $300 million of the proceeds in Act III Ventures, a new fund he founded to back emerging restaurant chains.
The fund's first big bet was on Cava, which went public at a nearly $5 billion valuation in June 2023.
Shaich owned nearly 10% of Cava when the company IPO'd but has since sold more than half his shares for at least $600 million (pre-tax).

name: Sergei Makhlai
forbes_bio: Sergei Makhlai is co-owner of Togliattiazot, one of Russia's biggest producers of nitrogen fertilizers.
In 2011 he became the head of Togliattiazot after his father, Vladimir Makhlai, stepped down as the company's CEO.
In May 2019, the Russian government opened an investigation against him and his father for large-scale fraud. In July that year, they were each sentenced in absentia to nine years in prison.
The Makhlais, who deny wrongdoing, do not live in Russia and have thus not served any time.

name: Xiong Xuqiang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2012-2019); Hurun Global (2014-2019); Hurun China (2007-2018)
forbes_bio: Real estate developer Xiong Xuqiang founded his current flagship business Yinyi Real Estate after turning around a money-losing canned food factory.
Xiong also owns a stake in semiconductor materials maker Ningbo Kangqiang Electronics.
Xiong is a former top Communist Party official in the eastern China city of Ningbo where Yinyi Real Estate is headquartered.

name: Saket Burman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun India (2017-2020)
forbes_bio: Saket Burman is the fifth-generation member of the storied Burman clan that founded Dabur, India's fourth-largest consumer goods company.
He inherited a minority stake and a board seat in Dabur from his father Siddharth Burman, who died in 2015.
Other assets he owns include property and financial investments.
Saket founded and sold several companies. He is currently focused on building his family office.
He was appointed vice chairman of Dabur in 2022.
forbes_facts: He is a member of Mumbai Angels, a group that backs startups.
He shuttles between homes in Dubai, London and Delhi.

name: Ed Hallen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2023)
forbes_bio: Ed Hallen is cofounder and chief product officer of Klaviyo, which sells marketing automation software.
The firm raised more than $500 million from venture capitalists and made a gross profit of $675 million in 2024.
Klaviyo was one of the first tech firms to test the IPO waters after a market downturn; it went public in 2023.
In 2017, Hallen stepped away from a full-time role at Klaviyo to start HR automation firm Team Engine, but rejoined in 2021 as chief product officer.
Before Klaviyo, he worked at a business analytics software firm. He holds a degree in systems engineering from the University of Virginia and an MBA from MIT.

name: Katrina Lake
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Hurun Global (2021); Hurun Global U40 (2021)
forbes_bio: Katrina Lake is the founder and CEO of Stitch Fix, an online personal-shopping service.
Lake started the company out of her Cambridge apartment in 2011 while completing her Harvard MBA.
Stitch Fix leverages data science and human stylists to send personalized outfits to a customer's door.
Lake took the company public in 2017 at age 34, becoming the youngest female founder ever to lead an IPO; she owns a 10% stake.
Stitch Fix now has over three million active customers and generated revenue of $1.6 billion in 2019.
forbes_facts: Lake sits on the boards of GrubHub and Glossier.

name: Faxiang Yu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023-2025); Forbes annual (2001-2024); Hurun Global (2018-2025); Hurun China (2005-2025)
forbes_bio: Yu Faxiang chairs Sunriver Holding Group, which was founded as a tourism business in in Hainan in 1992.
Sunriver Holding has stakes in animation company Zhejiang Sunriver Culture and highway construction firm Gourgen Traffic Construction.
Sunriver Holding has 5,000 employees with the total asset of 45 billion yuan, or $6.4 billion, according to the company's website.

name: Yan Junxu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2023); Hurun Global (2022-2023); Hurun China (2011-2023)
forbes_bio: Yan Junxiu is the founder and chairman of Titan Wind, a supplier of wind power generation equipment.
The company, founded in 2005, has expanded in Europe through acquisitions in Denmark and Germany.
Titan listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2010.
